prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: c025 (decay<=0.5, ignore_net_degree halved, adam scheme, per-net weight cap 15.68) is the strongest robust candidate; modestly relaxing the cap to ~31.4 (x2) lets the worst-path nets keep enough weight to further reduce WNS without losing the broad TNS gains, staying within the tested trend that relaxing the cap improved all cases.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.761 robust(mean-std)=+0.237 min_case=+0.231 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.267 dWNS=+27.7% dTNS=+25.9% overflow~86
  bp-ng45: score=+0.231 dWNS=+25.6% dTNS=+21.0% overflow~103
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.264 dWNS=+17.2% dTNS=+32.3% overflow~129
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis holds: all three cases valid, positive score, robust mean +0.237, min +0.231. Relaxing the cap improved WNS and TNS broadly—bp_fe-ng45 shows the largest TNS gain (+32.3%) with WNS +17.2%, while ariane133 and bp show balanced ~25% gains. Mechanism: higher per-net weight cap lets worst-path nets retain influence, tightening WNS without sacrificing TNS. Overflow (~86–129) stays moderate. Next step: test cap=31.4 directly against c025 across seeds to confirm the x2 relaxation preserves robustness and doesn't inflate overflow.
